Combined with the broad, pilot-dependent spectroscopy menu and acknowledged overlap risks in a heterogeneous mixed-medium system, this means the study is still best viewed as a specialist screening framework needing further narrowing or mirrored assignment controls before stronger donor-specific inference. (2) The card now more clearly narrows intended conclusions to descriptive cobalt-linked screening, which helps with overinterpretation risk. (3) However, the isotope control is still not mirrored on the TEA side, so donor-specific CO2-derived assignment remains asymmetrically bounded. Decision therefore remains revise, but on stronger footing than in the prior review."}],"overall":"Using only the supplied record, all six candidates remain plausible transfer-based research options for H05 rather than direct Co-bpy demonstrations. On re-review, E25, E26, E27, and E29 are shortlist-worthy because their questions are bounded and their controls are now adequate for the conclusions they actually claim. E26 changed from revise to shortlist because the prior asymmetry in isotope and cobalt-absent controls was explicitly corrected on the TEA side as well as the TEOA side. E28 and E30 should still be retained but revised: both have real value, but their strongest intended donor-mechanistic discrimination still depends on pilot-qualified, partly underspecified, or asymmetrically assignment-bounded observables. Across all cards, the key preserved caution is that TEA versus TEOA is a bundled chemical substitution, not a single microscopic variable, so product or spectral differences can support donor-linked chemistry without uniquely proving a catalyst-linked CO2 adduct or excluding cobalt-state and medium effects."}
